summary:
IGNIS is an AI-assisted space fire intelligence research platform designed to make spacecraft fire-safety research more accessible, structured, and actionable. Developed around NASA's Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) research, IGNIS brings together investigation discovery, scientific data exploration, evidence comparison, and research insights within a unified web-based platform.

Fire behaves differently in microgravity, where the absence of normal buoyancy-driven convection changes flame behaviour, airflow, and combustion dynamics. Understanding these differences is essential for protecting astronauts, spacecraft, and future space missions.

IGNIS addresses this challenge by transforming complex research records into an accessible intelligence environment. Users can explore spacecraft fire investigations, examine available experimental data, compare research conditions, and identify relevant scientific findings. The platform also distinguishes between measured datasets and metadata-only records to maintain transparency and prevent unsupported conclusions.

By bridging space-science research and accessible digital intelligence, IGNIS aims to support better-informed research, improve understanding of spacecraft fire risks, and contribute to safer future space exploration.
details:
IGNIS (Intelligent Spacecraft Fire Safety Research & Intelligence Platform) is an AI-assisted research platform developed to improve how spacecraft fire-safety investigations and scientific evidence are discovered, explored, analysed, and compared.

How It Works

IGNIS integrates research from NASA's Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) database into a unified web-based environment. Users can explore spacecraft fire-related investigations, examine available experimental information, navigate scientific research profiles, and compare relevant investigation conditions.

The platform features several interconnected modules, including an Overview Dashboard, Investigation Explorer, Scientific Intelligence, Investigations, Comparison, and Earth-based Research. Its intelligence capabilities use AI integration to assist with interpreting research information and presenting relevant insights. The system also distinguishes between records containing numerical experimental datasets and those containing metadata or supporting research only, helping users understand the limitations of available evidence.

Benefits and Intended Impact

Fire behaviour in microgravity differs significantly from that on Earth. Changes in buoyancy, airflow, flame propagation, and combustion dynamics create unique challenges for spacecraft fire safety.

IGNIS aims to make complex space-science research more accessible and understandable. By connecting research records, experimental information, and AI-assisted intelligence in one platform, it can help researchers, students, and space enthusiasts investigate potential fire-related risks, identify relevant evidence, and develop a better understanding of spacecraft fire behaviour.

Its long-term vision is to contribute to more informed spacecraft fire-safety research and support the development of safer future space missions.

Technology and Development Tools

The platform was developed using:

  • Python – Backend development and research data processing.
  • Flask – Web application framework and API routing.
  • HTML5, CSS3 and JavaScript – Interactive frontend and user interface.
  • Google Gemini API – AI-assisted research interpretation and intelligence.
  • NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) – Scientific research data source.
  • Git and GitHub – Version control and source-code management.
  • Vercel – Cloud deployment and public project accessibility.

Creativity and Innovation

IGNIS goes beyond presenting static scientific documents. It transforms scattered research information into an interactive intelligence platform that connects investigation discovery, data exploration, evidence comparison, and AI-assisted interpretation.

A key design principle is scientific transparency. Rather than generating artificial measurements or presenting unsupported conclusions, IGNIS communicates data availability and distinguishes actual experimental measurements from metadata-based research profiles.

Factors Considered

During development, our team considered the scientific complexity of microgravity combustion, the availability and reliability of NASA research records, data integrity, AI-generated information accuracy, accessibility, usability, and the importance of clearly communicating research limitations.

IGNIS is currently a research prototype intended to support scientific exploration and investigation, rather than replace certified spacecraft fire-detection or suppression systems.
